title: Ebola treatments trial begins in DR Congo
facts: The World Health Organization announced the beginning of a trial of potential treatments for Ebola in DR Congo.
The first patient has been enrolled in the clinical trial in the Democratic Republic of Congo.
The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo is caused by the Bundibugyo virus species.
There are currently no approved vaccines or treatments specifically for the Bundibugyo Ebola species.
The Ebola treatments trial is sponsored by the World Health Organization.
The Institut National de Recherche Biomédicale in DR Congo is co-ordinating the trial alongside international partners.
The current Ebola outbreak in DR Congo began in May 2026.
The World Health Organization declared the Ebola situation in DR Congo a public health emergency.
The World Health Organization confirmed 1,460 Ebola cases in DR Congo as of July 1, 2026.
The World Health Organization reported 452 deaths from Ebola in DR Congo as of July 1, 2026.
Uganda reported 20 confirmed cases and two deaths from Ebola.
The Ebola outbreak in DR Congo is primarily concentrated in South Kivu, North Kivu, and Ituri provinces.
A pregnant woman tested positive for Ebola in Tshopo province after dying in Ituri.
Public gatherings were banned in Tshopo, Haut-Uele, Bas-Uele, and Kinshasa to prevent disease transmission.
The number of diagnostic testing laboratories for Ebola in the region was increased from four to ten.
